text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index ended at a record closing high for the fifth session in a row on Monday as continued strength on Wall Street and a more relaxed peception of the British inflation outlook boosted shares. Dealers said the domestic economic picture for the FTSE remained bullish and the market could scale even loftier peaks as long as Wall Street maintained its firm tone. The FTSE 100 index of leading shares hit a record of 4,440.8 in morning trade and ended at 4,437.4, 17.1 points firmer.

FRANKFURT - Germany's blue-chip DAX index ended bourse trade at a new closing high on Monday with sentiment lifted by Friday's strong close on Wall Street above 7,000 points, firmer debt and a stable, if lower, dollar. At the end of the floor-trade session the DAX index stood at 3,436.07 points, up 59.87 points an all-time closing high for the index. In post-bourse trade the index rose 7.26 to 3,426.77.

PARIS - Paris shares scraped to a fourth consecutive record close on Monday although they finished well below their session highs. Traders said foreign funds were entering the market, offsetting some profit-taking on the market's gains. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 0.93 point at 2,709.21.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed at a record high, rising for the fifth day in a row, but the blue-chip Swiss Market Index slipped from the day's high of almost 4,700 points on late profit-taking. Dealers said firming stocks on Wall Street, soaring futures on government bonds and technicals were behind the rise. Foreign investors showed lively interest in Novartis, insurer Winterthur and bank shares in high turnover, they said.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) reached a record high of 2,959.03 points, up 20.59 points from Friday's close.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended moderately lower on Monday, hurt by a spate of bad news for Japan's biggest broker Nomura Securities Co Ltd and uncertainty over the country's financial reforms, brokers said. Some also attributed the fall to technical reasons, prompted by sales in futures contracts ahead of the March options and futures settlement later this week. The Nikkei 225 average lost 84.85 points to 18,113.89.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong blue chips ended weak on Monday as concerns that interest rates may move higher over coming weeks prompted investors to shun interest rate sensitive stocks and turn to China-related issues. The Hang Seng Index closed on a loss of 68.59 points at 13,268.76.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market secured strong gains by the close on Monday with the banks showing the way higher as both U.S. and local bond markets rallied. The All Ordinaries index closed 23.4 points higher at 2,461.9.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended firmly up on Monday as the market build-up to Wednesday's budget began in earnest, dealers said. After a bout of weakness in the morning both the all-share and industrials indices recovered and by mid-afternoon were steaming ahead. Dealers are braced for a volatile week as the close-out of the futures contract is fast approaching and derivatives traders are rushing to shore-up their positions, leaving the market open to steep swings.
The all-share index ended up 29.4 points to 7,091.3 as industrials jumped 75.4 points to 8,327.0. The local gold index lost 12.5 points to 1,404.4.
